evaluation_scope: Empirical Volunteer Webcam Usability and Latency Verification
disclaimer: Volunteer trials reflect monocular computer vision tracking usability and system latency. Because clinical physical therapist annotations were not acquired for these live webcam recordings, results are reported for tracking stability, repetition cadence, and view classification robustness without asserting validated clinical technique accuracy.
hardware_setup: Logitech C920 1080p RGB Webcam (USB 3.0), Chrome 129 WebGL, Windows 11

sessions.usability_notes: Clean tracking; parallel squat depth recognized smoothly.

sessions.view_gating_behavior: Knee valgus rule appropriately suppressed; sagittal depth evaluated.
sessions.usability_notes: Far leg occluded as expected; view gating prevented spurious valgus warnings.

warnings_issued: Squat deeper for full range of motion
sessions.usability_notes: Mild landmark jitter in ankle in low light; Kalman filter smoothed trajectory.
Bilateral arm tracking steady; concentric/eccentric phases clearly demarcated.
Backlight silhouetted participant; 1 rep missed inflection threshold.

aggregate_summary.system_usability_verdict: Real-time edge feedback is stable and responsive at ~17.4 FPS without transmitting raw video; view gating effectively suppresses out-of-plane rules under real webcam angles.
